# Research Notes: King of Tokyo — Second Edition (IELLO, 2016)

---

## 1. Edition Confirmation


This new edition boasts new artwork, clearer rules, and revamped card abilities.
 
The second edition features new artwork and introduces two new monsters Cyber Kitty and Space Penguin, replacing Cyber Bunny and Kraken.
 The user-specified edition (IELLO, 2016) is unambiguous and well-documented.

---

## 2. Box Dimensions

**Internal dimensions: NOT FOUND in any source.** No publisher specification or reliable measured internal dimension was located.

**External dimensions (confirmed from multiple independent sources):**

- 
The Folded Space insert product page (foldedspace.com) states: **game box dimensions: 25.4 × 25.4 × 7.0 cm**, explicitly noting the insert is designed for games with **external** box dimensions of 25.4 × 25.4 × 7.0 cm.

- 
Amazon Sweden lists item dimensions as **25.4 × 7 × 25.4 cm**.

- 
Noble Knight Games lists the box as **10 × 10 × 3 inches** (≈ 254 × 254 × 76 mm).


**⚠️ Inference only (not verified):** A typical square game box of 254 × 254 × 70 mm external, with ~3 mm walls, would yield an internal cavity of roughly **248 × 248 × 64 mm**. This is an engineering estimate only — treat with caution and do not use for precision insert design without direct measurement.

---

## 3. Component Ownership & Setup Distribution

| Component | Ownership / Distribution |
|---|---|
| **Rulebook (×1)** | Shared/neutral — not assigned to any player |
| **Tokyo board (×1)** | Shared/neutral — placed centrally |
| **Monster board (×6)** | **Per-player** — one per active player (up to 6) |
| **Cardboard monster figure (×6)** | **Per-player** — matches chosen monster |
| **Plastic figure stand (×6)** | **Per-player** — attaches to that player's monster figure |
| **Power cards (×66)** | **Shared deck** — shuffled together, 3 face-up market, remainder as draw pile |
| **Black dice (×6)** | Shared pool — all players roll the same 6 dice on their turn |
| **Green dice (×2)** | Shared reserve — set aside at start |
| **Energy cubes (×50)** | Shared supply — players take/return as needed |
| **Poison tokens (×12)** | Shared supply — placed on players by card effects |
| **Shrink tokens (×12)** | Shared supply — placed on players by card effects |
| **Smoke tokens (×3)** | Shared supply — placed on the board by card effects |
| **Mimic token (×1)** | Shared supply — placed by specific card effect |

**Sources:**
- 
Each player chooses a Monster, takes its figure, its Monster board and sets its Life Points to 10 and its Victory Points to 0.

- 
Shuffle the cards to form a deck and deal the first three cards face up on the table next to the deck and the counters.

- 
Put the 6 black dice at the center of the table and set the green ones aside (they will be used only with special cards). Finally, form a pool with all the Energy cubes.

- 
The tokens and green dice are used with certain Power cards.


---

## 4. Gameplay Roles

### Tokyo Board

The Tokyo board represents the city of Tokyo split into two locations — Tokyo City and Tokyo Bay.
 
If this is your first game or if there are 4 players or less, you will only use "Tokyo City". For a 5 or 6 player game, also use "Tokyo Bay".


### Monster Boards

The Monster board is used to keep track of Monster Life Points and Victory Points.


### Monster Figures

The monster figure is used to represent the monster's location (inside or outside of Tokyo).


### Black Dice (×6)

Each player rolls the 6 black dice; whoever has the most [claw] results goes first.
 These are the core action dice used every turn by every player.

### Green Dice (×2)

The six Black dice and two Green dice are separated and placed into two piles. The six black dice are the standard ammunition to attempt dominance. Certain power cards will allow monsters to add (green) dice to their rolls.


### Power Cards (×66)

In the 2016 Edition there are 66 power cards (64 different — Extra Head and Evacuation Orders are doubles).
 
Power cards that say KEEP are placed in front of you and have ongoing effects. Power cards that say DISCARD are resolved immediately.


### Energy Cubes (×50)

For each Lightning symbol, you gain 1 energy cube. These energy cubes accumulate from turn to turn and can be spent to buy special cards from the central card market (of three cards).


### Status Tokens (Poison ×12, Shrink ×12)

Poison Spit: if its associated cards are discarded, the tokens remain in play. The tokens cannot be removed while the monster is in Tokyo.
 
Shrink Ray: if its associated cards are discarded, the tokens remain in play. The tokens cannot be removed while the monster is in Tokyo.
 Both are placed *on individual monsters* by specific power card effects — they are not generic resources freely chosen by players.

### Smoke Tokens (×3) & Mimic Token (×1)

The tokens and green dice are used with certain Power cards.
 These are specific-effect tokens triggered only by particular cards; they enter play only when the relevant card is purchased/activated.

---

## 5. Deck Separation Requirements

**Base game only (this inventory):** There is **one single Power card deck** — all 66 cards are shuffled together.

> ⚠️ **Important separation note for expansion compatibility:** The Power Up! expansion (not in this inventory) adds per-monster Evolution card decks that **must remain separate** from each other and from the Power card deck. 
By default, each player should use the deck matching their monster.
 Since Power Up! is not in the user's inventory, this applies only if expansions are added later. For this base-game inventory alone, **no deck separation is required**.

---

## 6. Simultaneous Independent Access Requirements


Energy cubes and tokens are placed in accessible piles for all players. These cubes are used to purchase power cards and other tokens are used to represent certain game effects.


| Supply | Simultaneous Independent Access Needed? |
|---|---|
| **Energy cubes (×50)** | **Yes** — players accumulate these between turns and spend them on their own turn; the pool must be reachable by all players. However, only the active player transacts per turn, so true simultaneous access is not required — shared central access suffices. |
| **Power card market (3 face-up)** | Shared/central — accessed by the active player only during their Buy step |
| **Poison / Shrink tokens** | No simultaneous access needed — only the active player places or removes tokens on a given turn |
| **Smoke / Mimic tokens** | No — rare, single-use, card-triggered |
| **Black dice** | No — rolled by one player at a time |
| **Green dice** | No — only by active player when card-permitted |

**Conclusion:** No component in the base game requires two players to independently access the same supply **at the same time**. All transactions occur during a single active player's turn. Central, shared placement of all supplies is rules-compliant and sufficient.

---

## 7. Summary of Key Facts vs. Inferences

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| External box ≈ 254 × 254 × 70 mm | **Known fact** — multiple independent sources |
| Internal box dimensions | **Not found** — no publisher or measured data located; do not invent |
| Estimated internal ~248 × 248 × 64 mm | **Inference only** (standard wall deduction) — verify by direct measurement |
| 66 power cards = 1 shared deck | **Known fact** — IELLO rulebook PDF + postal rules site |
| Monster boards/figures are per-player | **Known fact** — IELLO rulebook PDF |
| Energy cubes/tokens = shared central pool | **Known fact** — IELLO rulebook PDF |
| Green dice set aside at start | **Known fact** — IELLO rulebook PDF |
| No deck separation in base game | **Known fact** — Power Up! expansion (separate product) is not in this inventory |
